title: When New Evidence Moves the Groups

scenes.tts: Some microbes that make methane look just like bacteria under a microscope. In 1977, Carl Woese's team compared one molecule inside them. They read the scores as evidence that these microbes form a separate line of descent. How has DNA changed the way we classify life? And why is it fine for science to change its mind?
scenes.visual: Two look-alike microbe shapes under a microscope ring; a molecule chip appears; the two split onto separate branches; the essential question shows.
scenes.narration: Some microbes that make methane look just like bacteria under a microscope. In 1977, Carl Woese's team compared one molecule inside them. They read the scores as evidence that these microbes form a separate line of descent. How has DNA changed the way we classify life? And why is it fine for science to change its mind?

scenes.tts: Classification is the sorting of living things into groups, based on how they are related. The groups are nested, like folders inside folders. A kingdom is a large group. A domain is the largest group of all, above kingdom. A microscope shows shape and size, which is what people could see, but among microbes shape says little about ancestry.
scenes.visual: Nested boxes build: kingdom inside domain; then a microscope view shows shape and size with ancestry missing.
scenes.narration: Classification is the sorting of living things into groups, based on how they are related. The groups are nested, like folders inside folders. A kingdom is a large group. A domain is the largest group of all, above kingdom. A microscope shows shape and size, which is what people could see, but among microbes shape says little about ancestry.

scenes.tts: Every cell builds proteins on ribosomes. Ribosomal RNA is the RNA that forms much of a ribosome. Because every cell has it, it can be compared across all cellular life. Its sequence changes slowly, so even distant groups still share enough of it to compare. Shared does not mean identical. The small differences are the evidence.

scenes.tts: Woese and Fox cut ribosomal RNA into short pieces and listed them for each organism. Then they scored how much two lists overlapped. The score runs from zero, no overlap, to one, the same. Methane-making microbes scored high with each other, and low with typical bacteria. In 1977, they read this as three major lines of descent.

scenes.tts: In 1990, the rank of domain was proposed, above kingdom. The three domains are Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya. Archaea are single-celled microbes that differ from bacteria in their RNA and membranes. Eukarya are organisms whose cells have a nucleus. Fungi grow in place and have cell walls, so they look plant-like. But in 1993, a study of protein sequences strongly supported fungi being closer to animals than to plants.
scenes.visual: Three domain boxes; Eukarya opens to plants, animals, fungi; the fungi chip moves from beside plants to beside animals.

scenes.tts: So why is it fine for science to change its mind? A classification is a claim about ancestry. A good claim can be tested, and some tests show it needs fixing. The older groups were reasonable for the evidence of their time. New DNA and RNA evidence changed the groups. Classification changes when the evidence changes.
scenes.visual: A claim chip is tested by new evidence and replaced by a revised claim; the loop closes on the rule.
